transcript.text: my belling cooker keeps burnin stuff 1 day then next day its undercookd on same temp. been like it a cuple months. thermastat??

To answer your question: yes, it is very likely a thermostat issue, but on modern ovens this is usually an electronic 'temperature sensor' rather than a mechanical dial. The symptom of alternating between burning and undercooking suggests the oven isn't reading its own heat correctly—it thinks it's one temperature when it's actually another. To narrow this down, I need to know if your cooker has a digital display with buttons or physical dials/knobs? This tells me whether we are looking at an electronic sensor fault (most common) or a mechanical thermostat drift.
its got proper knobs and little orange lights, no display or buttons. mines a 10 yr old belling double oven, only the main oven does it, the top oven and grill are fine

The most likely cause is indeed the internal oven thermostat. On these older units, the bimetallic strip inside can wear out over 10 years, causing the oven to swing between running too hot (burning) and cutting off too early (undercooking). To confirm this, please place an independent oven thermometer on the middle rack, set the oven to 180°C, and check the reading after 20 minutes. If it shows a significantly different temperature (e.g., over 200°C or under 160°C), the thermostat is faulty and needs replacing.
i dont have a thermomiter sorry. is there anything else i can check? the knob is a bit wobbly if that helps

The wobbly knob is a common side effect of the internal selector switch wearing out after 10 years, but it doesn't explain the temperature swings. Since you can't use a thermometer, the most practical check is to bake something simple like a tray of potatoes or a cake at your usual setting and time it carefully. If it consistently takes much longer than normal (undercooking) or burns on the outside while raw inside despite correct timing, this suggests the thermostat is failing to regulate the heat accurately. Given the age and symptoms, checking the oven thermostat is the most likely fix.
ok i can try baking something and timing it. should i be doing anything else, like is the door ok or the fan? i do sometimes put stuff in before its warmed up if that matters

Regarding your questions: the door seal is unlikely to cause this specific day-to-day swing unless it's visibly torn or leaking steam, and the fan (if you have a fan oven) would usually cause uneven cooking rather than consistent over/under-baking. Putting food in before it's warmed up will make things undercook initially but won't explain why it burns on other days at the same setting. Given the age of your cooker and the wobbly knob, the most likely culprit is a failing thermostat or its associated selector switch contacts. Since you don't have a thermometer, please proceed with that baking test we discussed: bake something simple like potatoes or a cake at your usual temperature and time it carefully against a known good recipe. If it consistently takes much longer than normal (undercooking) or burns on the outside while raw inside despite correct timing, this suggests the thermostat is failing to regulate heat accurately. In that case, you will need an engineer to check the oven thermostat or selector switch.
